"'''Congratulations'''" is a song by American musician [[Post Malone]] featuring American rapper [[Quavo]]. The song, at first released as a promotional single from Malone's debut [[studio album]] ''[[Stoney (album)|Stoney]]'' (2016) on November 4, 2016,<ref name="Complex">{{cite web|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2016/11/post-malone-new-song-congratulations-feat-quavo|title=Post Malone and Quavo connect on "Congratulations"|publisher=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|accessdate=November 10, 2016}}</ref> was released on January 31, 2017, as the fifth official single from the album.<ref name=FMQB>{{cite web|url= http://fmqb.com/Article.asp?id=16691 |title=Available for Airplay |publisher=FMQB |archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20170124182333/http://fmqb.com/Article.asp?id=16691|archivedate=January 24, 2017 |accessdate=January 24, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Malone and Quavo wrote the song with Carl Rosen and producers [[Metro Boomin]], [[Frank Dukes]], and [[Louis Bell]]. A remix, which includes an additional feature from fellow American rapper [[Future (rapper)|Future]], was released on June 16, 2017.

"Congratulations" is a song by American musician Post Malone featuring American rapper Quavo. The song, at first released as a promotional single from Malone's debut studio album Stoney (2016) on November 4, 2016, was released on January 31, 2017, as the fifth official single from the album. Malone and Quavo wrote the song with Carl Rosen and producers Metro Boomin, Frank Dukes, and Louis Bell. A remix, which includes an additional feature from fellow American rapper Future, was released on June 16, 2017.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
Producers [[Frank Dukes]], [[Metro Boomin]], and [[Louis Bell]] began working with Post Malone on tracks for his [[Stoney (album)|debut album]] after the success of the single "[[White Iverson]]." During the writing process, they were watching the [[2016 Summer Olympics]] and were inspired to create a triumphant song. At one point during the session, Post's manager Dre London shouted 'congratulations,' inspiring the chorus of the song.<ref>{{Cite AV media|url=https://www.redbull.com/ca-en/videos/in-conversation-with-frank-dukes|title=In conversation with Frank Dukes|date=December 18, 2019|type=video|language=en-CA|publisher=[[Red Bull Music Academy]]|minutes=40:58-45:00}}</ref>

Post Malone debuted the track while performing in Austin, Texas in September 2016, two months before the song's official release.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/513653-post-malone-performs-new-quavo-collaboration-contratulations-in-austin-new-video|title=Post Malone Performs New Quavo Collaboration, "Congratulations," In Austin|website=HNHH |date=24 September 2016|access-date=January 18, 2017}}</ref>

On May 9, 2017, the track was performed to Post Malone by a [[Mariachi|mariachi band]], commissioned by Indonesian rapper [[Rich Brian]].

On June 16, 2017, the official remix was released featuring an additional verse from [[Future (rapper)|Future]].
sections.text:
Producers Frank Dukes, Metro Boomin, and Louis Bell began working with Post Malone on tracks for his debut album after the success of the single "White Iverson." During the writing process, they were watching the 2016 Summer Olympics and were inspired to create a triumphant song. At one point during the session, Post's manager Dre London shouted 'congratulations,' inspiring the chorus of the song.

Post Malone debuted the track while performing in Austin, Texas in September 2016, two months before the song's official release.

On May 9, 2017, the track was performed to Post Malone by a mariachi band, commissioned by Indonesian rapper Rich Brian.

On June 16, 2017, the official remix was released featuring an additional verse from Future.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: The song is written in the key of [[F-sharp major|F♯ major]] with a tempo of 110 beats per minute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0178282|title = Congratulations| website=Musicnotes |date = 28 September 2017}}</ref>

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The song's accompanying music video premiered on January 23, 2017, on Post Malone's [[Vevo]] account on [[YouTube]]. The music video was directed by James DeFina.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/515983-post-malone-feat-quavo-congratulations-video-new-video|title=Post Malone Feat. Quavo "Congratulations" Video|website=HNHH |date=23 January 2017|access-date=January 23, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SC4xMk98Pdc&t|title=Post Malone - Congratulations ft. Quavo|website=[[YouTube]] |date=23 January 2017 |accessdate=January 23, 2017}}</ref> It features cameo appearances from [[Murda Beatz]], [[Metro Boomin]], [[Frank Dukes]], and fellow members of the [[Migos]] crew. {{As of|2025|6}}, the music video has been viewed over 1.6 billion times.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SC4xMk98Pdc|title=Post Malone - Congratulations ft. Quavo|publisher=PostMaloneVEVO|date=January 23, 2017|accessdate=June 2, 2017|via=YouTube}}</ref>
sections.text: The song's accompanying music video premiered on January 23, 2017, on Post Malone's Vevo account on YouTube. The music video was directed by James DeFina. It features cameo appearances from Murda Beatz, Metro Boomin, Frank Dukes, and fellow members of the Migos crew. {{As of|2025|6}}, the music video has been viewed over 1.6 billion times.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: The song peaked at number eight on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], becoming Post Malone's second top 20 hit, following his debut single, "[[White Iverson]]", and first top 10 hit, and has spent a total of 50 weeks on the chart. The song was later certified [[RIAA certification|Diamond (11× Platinum)]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA) for combined sales and streaming equivalent units of over 11 million units in the United States.
sections.text: The song peaked at number eight on the US Billboard Hot 100, becoming Post Malone's second top 20 hit, following his debut single, "White Iverson", and first top 10 hit, and has spent a total of 50 weeks on the chart.
